title: Australia news LIVE: Pay rises, tax cuts
text:

This masthead’s chief political commentator James Massola has won press gallery journalist of the year for his insightful analysis of the internal machinations within both the Labor and Liberal parties.

You can read an example of Massola’s typical insightful journalism here in this cogent analysis of how the new right was reshaping the federal Liberal Party and modern politics.

This follows political correspondent Natassia Chrysanthos winning the award for young press gallery journalist of the year last week.

And with that happy news for all of us here, we bring tonight’s live coverage to a close. We will be back tomorrow morning to continue our live coverage.

Less than 24 hours ago, the Coalition and the Greens teamed up to kick Labor’s lukewarm gambling ad crackdown to another committee.

So you’d think that not a single member of the Albanese government would be caught dead sitting at Canberra’s annual night of nights, the Midwinter Ball, at a table sponsored by none other than Sportstbet. But you’d be wrong!

To find out who supped with the gambling behemoth, read the full CBD column here.

Health Minister Mark Butler and wife Daniela Ritorto haven’t heard the PM’s speech ahead of time, but what they’re really looking forward to is Opposition Leader Angus Taylor’s debut.

“Sussan Ley overperformed last year. She was hilarious,” Butler said.

Are they looking forward to anything else?

“Just spending the night together,” said Ritorto, who is wearing her sister’s label, Acler. “Damn, I should have said that,” Butler lamented.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, his wife Jodie Haydon and Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence Richard Marles look like they are enjoying themselves early while Minister for Employment and Workplace Relations Amanda Rishworth can barely contain her elation.

Meanwhile, Marles’ son, professional cage fighter Sam Marles eschews his trademark scowl for a charming smile. Possibly because his father introduced him to the prime minister with the words: “He’s my date tonight.”

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, sporting a bowtie, with wife Jodie Haydon wearing a floral gown by the Australian designer Leo Lin, were one of the later arrivals at the ball.

“Contemporary Australian designer Leo Lin loaned the Sofia gown to Jodie to wear to the Midwinter Ball,” the PM said.

The dress is from the label’s current Prefall collection and features intricate hand-embellishments, he noted.

The teals have entered as a united front, despite their splits over whether to join the new party, Community Strong Australia.

Party founders Zali Steggall and Allegra Spender needed to take a selfie before they could be asked who they were wearing.

Steggall pulled her jumpsuit out of the back of her closet, and Spender is wearing her mother’s brand, Carla Zampatti.

She said it was “beautiful” to wear her mother’s brand and that she was very proud to do so.

Nicolette Boele, who is yet to reveal her future with the party, is wearing an $18 black-sequin dress bought from a Vinnies store in the Sydney suburb of Chatswood. Her handbag was $5.

A group shot of Labor MPs and senators.

Liberal senator Claire Chandler has been wearing flats all week to prepare for donning some heels this evening.Her forest-green dress from Portmans hugs her baby bump.“Given I’m six-months pregnant, I’m dressing for comfort,” she said.

Jamie King and Minister for Resources and Northern Australia Madeleine King.

Louise Clegg and Opposition Leader Angus Taylor arrived at 7.15pm in the Marble Hall.

Asked what she was wearing Mrs Taylor said it was a black Country Road top over a pewter coloured skirt, the brand of which escaped her.
